nodes.label: Learning from the Self-future: On-policy Self-distillation for dLLMs
nodes.author: Yifu Luo, Zeyu Chen, Haoyu Wang, Xinhao Hu, Yuxuan Zhang, Zhizhou Sha, Shiwei Liu
nodes.rationale: First OPSD framework tailored for diffusion LLMs, addressing fundamental incompatibilities between autoregressive-centric OPSD and arbitrary-order generation of dLLMs through self-generated answers as suffix conditioning and step-level divergence supervision.

nodes.label: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD)
nodes.rationale: Paradigm where a single model serves as both teacher and student using privileged information, enabling self-improvement without requiring a separate stronger teacher model.

nodes.label: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs)
nodes.rationale: Alternative to autoregressive LLMs that model language generation as iterative denoising process, enabling arbitrary-order generation and speed-up inference.

nodes.label: d-OPSD: Diffusion On-Policy Self-distillation
nodes.rationale: Novel OPSD framework specifically designed for dLLMs using self-generated answers as suffix conditioning and step-level divergence supervision instead of token-level.

nodes.label: Self-Teacher Construction via Suffix Conditioning
nodes.rationale: Core innovation: uses self-generated answers as suffix privileged information rather than prefix conditioning, enabling student to learn from 'self future-experience' and better aligning with on-policy nature and dLLM's bidirectional capability.

nodes.label: Step-Level Divergence Supervision
nodes.rationale: Shifts dense supervision from token-level to step-level, aligning with iterative denoising nature of dLLMs where only top-k most confident tokens among masked positions dictate state transitions.

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)
nodes.rationale: Existing post-training paradigm for LLMs using outcome rewards; suffers from sparse reward bottleneck and heavy computation overhead compared to OPSD.

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
nodes.rationale: Standard post-training approach; suffers from exposure bias when training distribution differs from inference distribution.

nodes.label: LLaDA-8B-Instruct
nodes.author: Nie et al., 2025
nodes.rationale: State-of-the-art dLLM used as base model for experiments; chosen over Dream due to output format consistency issues.

nodes.label: GSM8K: Grade School Math Benchmark
nodes.author: Cobbe et al., 2021
nodes.rationale: Mathematical reasoning benchmark used to evaluate d-OPSD performance.

nodes.label: MATH500: Mathematical Reasoning Benchmark
nodes.author: Lightman et al., 2023
nodes.rationale: Mathematical reasoning benchmark used to evaluate d-OPSD performance.

nodes.label: 4x4 Sudoku Puzzle Task
nodes.rationale: Planning task requiring constraint satisfaction; used to evaluate d-OPSD on non-mathematical reasoning.

nodes.label: Countdown (3 numbers) Task
nodes.rationale: Planning task requiring arithmetic operations to reach target; used to evaluate d-OPSD on planning problems.

nodes.label: diffu-GRPO
nodes.author: Zhao et al., 2025
nodes.rationale: RLVR baseline applying GRPO to dLLMs; d-OPSD achieves superior performance with ~10% of optimization steps.

nodes.label: VRPO: Variance-Reduced Policy Optimization
nodes.author: Zhu et al., 2025
nodes.rationale: RLVR baseline for dLLMs; compared against d-OPSD in reasoning performance evaluation.

nodes.label: d3LLM: Ultra-fast Diffusion LLM
nodes.author: Qian et al., 2026
nodes.rationale: Off-policy self-distillation approach for dLLMs using pseudo-trajectory; differs from d-OPSD by using static dataset answers and single forward pass rather than on-policy trajectories.

nodes.label: Overlap Top-K Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures proportion of tokens appearing in both student's and teacher's Top-K vocabulary distributions; used to explain why d-OPSD outperforms AR-style OPSD by providing more new knowledge.

nodes.label: Block-Diffusion Inference Strategy
nodes.author: Han et al., 2023; Arriola et al., 2025
nodes.rationale: Hybrid inference approach partitioning response into blocks with autoregressive decoding at block level and diffusion-style within blocks; used in d-OPSD experiments.

nodes.label: Per-Token Pointwise KL Clipping
nodes.rationale: Stabilization technique addressing skewed token-level divergence across vocabulary; ablation shows substantial performance improvement and training stability.

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.author: Hu et al., 2022
nodes.rationale: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method used in d-OPSD implementation with rank r=128 and scaling factor α=64.

nodes.label: Exposure Bias Problem
nodes.author: Bengio et al., 2015
nodes.rationale: Training-inference mismatch where model trains on ground truth but infers on its own generations; OPSD addresses this by using student's own samples.

nodes.label: Arbitrary-Order Generation
nodes.rationale: Key advantage of dLLMs over autoregressive models; enables non-left-to-right generation and suffix conditioning for privileged information.

nodes.label: Policy Collapse Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Observed failure mode where OPSD training degrades catastrophically after peak performance; hypothesized to stem from model-seeking behavior becoming overly narrow.

nodes.label: Pass@k Sampling Strategy
nodes.rationale: Sampling strategy keeping trajectories until correct answer occurs or iteration threshold met; shares computation overhead with RLVR group k rollouts.

nodes.label: Forward Process in dLLMs
nodes.rationale: Gradually corrupts clean input by replacing tokens with mask token; inverse of reverse process used during inference.

nodes.label: Reverse Process (Inference) in dLLMs
nodes.rationale: T-step iterative denoising from fully masked sequence to clean response; core inference mechanism of dLLMs.

nodes.label: Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence
nodes.rationale: Primary divergence measure for OPSD; reverse KL (model-seeking) outperforms forward KL (model-covering) in d-OPSD experiments.

nodes.label: Self-Teacher Construction
nodes.source_location: D.2 Toy Experiment Details and Examples
nodes.rationale: Prevents leaking final answers by clearing unmasked tokens when moving to new blocks, retaining only mask tokens in new blocks
